summary: Nicholas Justin Allen (1939–2020) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. Educated at Oxford, New College, and SOAS, he completed his doctorate under Rodney Needham. He held posts at Durham and Oxford, including Wolfson College.

Nicholas Roerich (1874–1947) worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Imperial Academy of Arts, later directing the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts.
Nicholas Witkowski specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at Stanford University in 2015 and served as a research fellow at the University of Tokyo as attested in 2017.
Nicholson T. Collier is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under the doctoral supervision of Paul J. Griffiths.

Nicola Bajetta is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied as a doctoral local researcher at the University of Hamburg, where he was also attested in 2026 as a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter.

Nicola Di Cosmo is a historian specializing in Sinology and Iranian/Central Asian studies who earned his PhD from Indiana University Bloomington. He held positions at Cambridge, Harvard, Columbia, the University of Canterbury, and the Institute for Advanced Study.

Nicolaas Johannes Krom (1883–1945) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (1913–1916) and held academic posts at Leiden University in 1919 and from 1925 to 1945.
Nicolaas van Wijk (1880–1942) was a linguist who studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1898–1903) and Moscow State University (~1903–1904). In 1913, he took up a post at Leiden University.
Nicolas Morrissey works in the fields of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Gregory Schopen (attested 2004) and holds a post at the University of Georgia.

Nicolas Revire works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Claudine Bautze-Picron and Peter Skilling, he studied at Silpakorn University (2012–2013) and held a post at Thammasat University, attested in 2016–2017.

Nicolas Sihlé specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant professor in the Department of Anthropology at the University of Virginia, where his affiliation is attested in 2010 and 2026.

Nicolas Tournadre is a linguist and Tibetologist who completed his PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Claude Hagège. He held academic posts at Paris 8, INALCO, the University of Virginia, and Aix-Marseille University.
Nicole Baden (born 1981) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Richard Baker and succeeded him in 2024.

Nicole Vandier-Nicolas (1906–1987) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She taught Chinese art at the École du Louvre (1966–1977) and served as professor of Chinese civilization at INALCO (~1969–1977).

Niels Ludvig Westergaard (1815–1878) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Christian Lassen at the University of Bonn. He spent his career at the University of Copenhagen, serving as professor from 1850 and rector from 1867 to 1868.
Nigel Allan specializes in history and archaeology. He succeeded Marianne Winder and held the post of Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust, attested in 1993.

Niharranjan Ray (1903–1981) was a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned doctorates at Calcutta and Leiden. He served as Bageswari Professor at the University of Calcutta and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

Nika Jovic is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Vienna, earning her Magistra der Philosophie under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes, and was taught by Géza Bethlenfalvy.

Nikita Yakovlevich Bichurin (1777–1853) was a scholar in Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Kazan Theological Academy and held a post at the Département asiatique from around 1826 to 1853.

Niklas Luhmann (1927–1998) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Freiburg, Bielefeld University, and Harvard University (~1960–1961). He held an academic post at Bielefeld University from around 1968 to 1993.
